title: Introduce OPA policy bridge for RBACv2 evaluation and KMS-usage metering
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context and motivation: We have an increasing number of RBACv2 rule variants and per-tenant KMS residency constraints which are difficult to evaluate consistently in multiple runtimes. This PR adds an OPA-based policy bridge that centralizes policy evaluation for RBACv2 and emits structured metering events for KMS usage. The bridge is implemented as a light-weight policy server library that can be linked into the runtime or deployed as a sidecar; it supports Rego templates for common tenancy patterns and a small runtime cache to avoid repeated expensive evaluations.

What this PR does (single-string description with checklist): 1) Adds pkg/policy/opa_bridge.go: OPA client wrapper + evaluation API. 2) Adds Rego templates under policies/templates/ for tenant-scoped role assertions and kms-consent rules. 3) Adds internal/kms/meter.go and middleware to produce per-request KMS-meter events (tenant, key, op, region) and emit audit payloads. 4) Introduces evaluation metrics (pkg/policy/eval_metrics.go) for latency, cache hit rate, and policy size. 5) Adds integration test coverage and an example in examples/opa/. 6) Adds docs and a migration guide for policy authors and infra teams. 7) Helm values for enabling the bridge in the rbac-policy-bundle chart.

Checklist: [x] design doc referenced (ENG-2413), [x] unit tests added, [x] integration test for KMS metering added, [x] docs and migration guide, [x] observability and SLI hooks, [x] rollback plan included.

Commits (high level): 7 commits: initial OPA client and shim; add Rego templates and policy examples; implement KMS metering middleware; metrics and cache; integration tests; docs and helm chart values; fix flaky test and CI tweaks.

Changed areas and rationale: - Policy evaluation: centralizing via OPA reduces drift between services that previously had ad-hoc evaluation code. Rego templates make it easier for compliance to express residency rules. - KMS metering: a standardized meter makes it possible to attribute KMS calls to tenants and regions for audit and billing. - Performance: evaluation cache and short-lived partial-result cache were introduced to keep average eval latency < 2ms for common fast-paths. Benchmarks included in the PR show a cold-eval median of ~8ms on a single x86 dev box and warm-eval median ~0.9ms with cache enabled.

Footnotes on security controls and compliance: The bridge validates that Rego policies include explicit residency assertions when required by feature gates. Policy templates include deny-by-default principals for cross-region key usage. Audit events from the KMS meter are signed and contain an immutable policy_fingerprint field for post-hoc verification.

Staged rollout and migration: We will deploy the bridge as a sidecar behind a feature flag (rbac.opa_bridge.enabled) and progressively flip canaries: dev -> staging (50%) -> production (10% subset with low QPS) -> full rollout over 7 days. Migration guide in docs/rbac/migration-guide.md explains how to translate legacy role bindings to the Rego helpers and how to validate equivalence with the back-compat shim.

Testing and CI notes: Integration tests initially failed in CI due to a mocked KMS stub mismatch; the test harness was updated and the failing check was rerun (integration-kms: rerun passed). Load bench scripts are in tests/bench/ and were used to verify eval latency and cache behavior.

Rollback plan: Feature flag can be toggled off; the sidecar is backward compatible and falls back to legacy evaluation code on severe errors. If KMS-metering emits malformed events, a short-lived kill-switch (rbac.kms_meter.disabled) prevents emissions while preserving decision flows.

Related work and references: ENG-2413 (design), SEC-78 (compliance review), earlier policy bundle PRs for residency enforcement.

review_comments: Rohit Singh: Overall looks good. Please add a microbenchmark for evaluation cache hit-rate and include p95 numbers (requested change).
Ava Martinez: Added bench script and p95 numbers to eval_metrics.go comments and to the docs. See tests/bench/benchmark_eval.sh (reply).

Ava Martinez: Rego templates now include a default deny-and-audit clause; added a new audit field policy_fingerprint for traceability (reply).
Diego Alvarez: Integration test failed in CI initially due to stub mismatch; re-ran and passed. Approving after green CI.
Rohit Singh: Approve. Left a minor nits comment about log level for policy failures.
Ava Martinez: Addressed nit, now using warn for transient OPA client errors and error for evaluation failures tied to deny decisions.
verification_steps: Integration: make test-integration (requires local KMS stub)
Bench: tests/bench/benchmark_eval.sh to reproduce eval latency numbers
Manual: enable rbac.opa_bridge.enabled in staging values and verify policy_fingerprint appears in audit events
release_notes: Adds OPA-based policy bridge for RBACv2 and standardized KMS-usage metering. Provides Rego templates to express tenant-scoped residency rules and denials for cross-region KMS usage. Opt-in via helm flag rbac.opa_bridge.enabled. Backwards compatible with legacy evaluation shims.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in helm values and monitor new metrics policy.eval.latency, policy.cache.hit_ratio, rbac.kms_meter.events_emitted. Watch for integration-kms errors during the first 24h of rollout. Can toggle rbac.opa_bridge.enabled=false to rollback.
risk_assessment: Medium: introduces new policy evaluation path that affects authorization decisions. Mitigations: staged rollout, feature flags, back-compat shim, and defensive default-deny templates. Audit signatures ensure post-deployment verification.
